question.prompt: Suppose \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. When the polynomial \(x^3 + x^2 + ax + b\) is divided by \(x - 1,\) the remainder is \(4.\) When the polynomial is divided by \(x - 2,\) the remainder is \(6.\) What is \(b - a?\)

solutions.title: Use remainders to form two equations
solutions.explanation:
The Remainder Theorem turns each given remainder into an equation: dividing a polynomial \(P(x)\) by \(x-c\) leaves remainder \(P(c)\).

For \(P(x)=x^3+x^2+ax+b\), the two conditions give
\[
P(1)=1+1+a+b=4,
\]
\[
P(2)=8+4+2a+b=6.
\]
Thus
\[
a+b=2,\qquad 2a+b=-6.
\]
Subtracting the first equation from the second gives \(a=-8\). Substituting into \(a+b=2\) gives \(b=10\). Therefore
\[
b-a=10-(-8)=\boxed{18},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

solutions.title: Substitute from the first remainder equation
